items.title: Rate-limit link creation per API key
items.body:
One API key created 50k links in an hour last week. We have no limit on link creation per key.

We should rate-limit link creation per API key and return `429` with a `Retry-After` header when the limit is hit.

decisions.statement: The team decided to use a shared Redis link cache with a 24-hour TTL instead of keeping in-process LRU caches with pub/sub invalidation.
The project decided to generate short codes as random 7-character base62 strings using secrets and retrying on collision.
Expired links return 410 Gone instead of 302 on redirects after their expiry time.

pending_proposals.statement: Replace the Redis link cache with an in-process LRU cache and pub/sub invalidation.
pending_proposals.note: PR #16 is not merged; this is a proposal, not a current decision

items.title: CSV export times out above 100k clicks
items.body:
Exporting clicks as CSV times out for any link with more than about 100k clicks.

The export builds the whole file in memory before sending it. It should stream rows instead.

items.title: Docs: explain how link expiry works
items.body:
Nobody can find how and when links expire. Support keeps answering the same questions: what happens after a link expires, whether expired links still count clicks, and whether editing a link resets its expiry.

We need a short doc that explains link expiry end to end.

items.title: Allow custom aliases for links
items.body:
Users want to choose a readable alias for a link, such as `/launch`, instead of a random code.

We would need to check aliases against existing codes, reserve paths we use ourselves, and decide which characters are allowed.

The redirect handler preserves short-code case end to end by removing the lowercasing step.

items.title: p99 redirect latency regressed after the Redis cache
items.body:
Since the Redis link cache shipped, p99 redirect latency went from 4 ms to 12 ms. Every redirect now makes a network hop to Redis, even for the hottest links.

Our setup has also changed since that decision: we now run 2 replicas in one region, not 3 replicas across 2 regions. We should revisit whether a shared cache is still worth the extra hop.

// 13 F5 triage inbox: triage Tasks with their issue, newest first. $status = '' for all.
// draft / approved_draft are written by Steward (M13) and the approve route.
MATCH (t:Task {type: 'triage'})-[:FOR]->(i:Issue)
WHERE $status = '' OR t.status = $status
RETURN t.id AS task_id, t.status AS status, t.at AS opened_at, t.claimed_by AS claimed_by,
       t.draft AS draft, t.approved_draft AS approved_draft, t.approved_by AS approved_by,
       t.approved_at AS approved_at,
       i.id AS issue_id, i.number AS number, i.title AS title, i.url AS url, i.state AS issue_state,
       left(coalesce(i.body, ''), 600) AS body
ORDER BY t.at DESC, i.number DESC
LIMIT $limit

// 09 F5 triage: decisions that AFFECT any of $modules (the modules where similar issues were
// fixed), with status and kind so the tool can keep proposed and superseded ones apart from
// current ones. Decisions below $min_confidence are left out.
UNWIND $modules AS mid
MATCH (d:Decision)-[:AFFECTS]->(m:Module {id: mid})
WHERE d.confidence >= $min_confidence
WITH d, collect(DISTINCT m.id) AS modules
RETURN d.id AS id, d.statement AS statement, d.status AS status, d.kind AS kind,
       d.confidence AS confidence, d.source_id AS source_id, d.source_url AS source_url, modules
ORDER BY size(modules) DESC, d.valid_from DESC
LIMIT $limit
